problem: Prior VLN work aligns whole instructions or sub-instructions to trajectories, so supervision stays at sentence level. Existing entity-region attempts lack direct, precise entity-phrase to landmark supervision (weak or parser-derived groundings).
motivation: Matching mentioned landmarks (objects/scenes) to visual observations is key to correct action decisions, but datasets only give coarse text-image alignment. Fine-grained, human-verified entity-landmark grounding could give direct supervision to pre-trained VLN models.
key_idea: Human-annotate entity-phrase to landmark-bounding-box pairs on R2R (GEL-R2R) and use them for an adaptive pre-training stage of HAMT with entity phrase prediction, landmark box prediction and entity-landmark contrastive alignment.
insight: Explicit entity-landmark supervision improves cross-modal attention (higher Effective Attention scores than HAMT, both e2l and l2e) and navigation, especially in unseen environments. In the ablation, position-only objectives (EPP, LBP) alone do not help (SR 65.8/65.6 vs 65.7 baseline), while feature-level contrastive ELSA does (66.3), and all three together are best (69.2), showing complementarity. Object and scene landmarks each help (66.8 / 66.7) and combining them is best, suggesting data volume is still limiting.
method: GEL-R2R dataset: human annotation of entity phrases and landmark bounding boxes in R2R panoramas (71,467 phrases, 150,183 boxes over train/val-seen/val-unseen). Labels use free text, coreference labels and one box per phrase per panorama; 43 qualified annotators plus expert revision. Panoramas are rotated to the next-action direction and matched to FG-R2R sub-instructions.

Base model: HAMT (LXMERT-style cross-modal transformer with hierarchical history encoder, ViT features), pre-trained with MLM, MRC, ITM, SAP and SPREL, all kept during adaptive pre-training to avoid forgetting.

Entity Phrase Prediction (EPP): averages landmark patch representations via mask M_s, then a 2-layer FFN and softmax predict a distribution over instruction token positions; cross-entropy against the entity mask M_z.
Landmark Bounding box Prediction (LBP): averages entity token embeddings via M_z, then an FFN and sigmoid regress box (x,y,w,h); loss is smooth-L1 plus GIoU (adapted from TransVG).

Entity-Landmark Semantic Alignment (ELSA): bidirectional InfoNCE-style contrastive loss (tau=0.07) between landmark patch and entity token output embeddings from the cross-modal encoder (from MDETR). Total loss is L_EPP + L_LBP + L_ELSA with all weights 1.0.

Fine-tuning: IL+RL as in HAMT; for R2R three augmentation settings (none, st style-transfer, smo semantic-masked synthesized environments, following EnvEdit); CVDN follows HAMT with navigator+oracle demonstrations.

setting.backbone: HAMT (LXMERT-style transformer with ViT-B/16 features), adaptively pre-trained then fine-tuned
setting.training_data: Adaptive pre-training on GEL-R2R train (14,039 instructions with entity-landmark annotations) plus PREVALENT augmented R2R data (pre-training tasks only), 200k iterations; fine-tuning on R2R or CVDN with IL+RL, optional st/smo environment augmentation
setting.observation: 36-view panoramic RGB with orientation angles, plus history of past panoramas
setting.privileged: none at test time (entity-landmark annotations used only in training)

results: GELA reaches R2R val-unseen SR 71 / SPL 65 and test-unseen SR 67 / SPL 62, beating HAMT (66/61 val-unseen, 65/60 test), and CVDN GP 5.86 val-unseen and 5.87 test versus HAMT's 5.13 and 5.58. The gains are largest in unseen environments; val-seen is comparable to HAMT on R2R.
limitations: GEL-R2R is small because human annotation is costly (>2000 h annotation), so performance likely is not saturated
Annotations only cover R2R (MP3D); the augmented data lacks grounding labels, and generalization beyond HAMT and R2R/CVDN is untested
NE gets worse than HAMT on val-unseen (3.11 vs 2.29) and ensembles are not compared
